name: grounding-two-pass-verbosity
withdrawalReason: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-20, never executed under this registration. The registered transport no longer exists: a live quota probe on 2026-10-20 showed unorouter's registered model nemotron-3.5-lightning:free answering 404 model_not_found (the slug was retired from the provider's catalogue - the same failure mode that killed the kiraai slugs), with both unorouter fallbacks answering 429 because the free tier allows only 5 requests per minute. The registration named that exact model in its singleVariable, so the study could never have measured what it was registered to measure: its whole design rests on a baseline of 0.200 verbosity stability measured on a transport that no longer serves it. The QUESTION is not withdrawn with it - the architecture question is still open and is re-registered against a transport that answers (see grounding-two-pass-verbosity-v2). This registration is kept byte-intact as the historical record of what was asked and of why it could not be run.
registeredVia: judge benchmark 2026-10-04, unorouter:nemotron-3.5-lightning:free (the default transport after #81)
question: The default judge is strongly sensitive to padding that adds no argument: verbosity inflation appends one sentence of pure emphasis to every line and the verdict moves in 16 of 20 usable fixtures (flipRate 0.800, stability 0.200 against a 0.95 gate). Style sophistication (0.706) and name removal (0.688) are nearly as bad. If the judge scored a grounded claim representation instead of the raw prose, would that padding stop moving the verdict, rather than the judge merely becoming sensitive to something else?
hypothesis: A two-pass judge - pass 1 extracts claims and classifies the supplied evidence, pass 2 scores the grounded representation - raises verbosity stability from the measured 0.200 to >= 0.40 without degrading agreement, ECE, position invariance, or provider reliability, accepting a measured latency and token cost.
singleVariable: JUDGE ARCHITECTURE: single-pass v5 prompt vs the two-pass grounding pipeline. Identical provider (unorouter), model (nemotron-3.5-lightning:free), fixtures, gates, temperature=0 and transport in both arms. The pass-2 system prompt is byte-identical to shipped v5; only the extraction pass and the user framing are new. The grounding rule is inherent to the architecture, not a wording tweak, so this is one variable and not stacked prompt edits.
order: serialized interleaved A,B,A,B; arms never run concurrently (provider budgets are shared and rate-limited)
designNote: Runs are preserved raw and may be appended across days in the same study dir; the verdict is always recomputed from all preserved runs against this same sealed rule. The earlier grounding-two-pass-unorouter study was INCONCLUSIVE solely because the transport measured below the registered reliability floor (usable runs 1/3 baseline, 0/3 candidate); this re-asks the architecture question on a transport now measuring 0.808 successRatio. The target is verbosity stability, NOT whitespace: measurement during registration (see docs/judge-runs/) found the whitespace probe was inert, so its published 0.667 was endpoint sampling noise mislabelled as formatting sensitivity and is not a usable baseline for anything. Verbosity is the largest genuine invariance failure on this pack and sits inside the selection priority docs/validation.md already declares ('verbosity robustness').

target.marginRationale: Baseline verbosity stability measured at 0.200 (16 flips across 20 usable probe calls, 2026-10-04 full pack). The gate requires >= 0.95, so the baseline misses by 0.75 and any real movement is unambiguous. 0.20 is well above the 0.02-0.07 per-arm run sd typical of this pack, so it is not noise, and it is far below the 0.75 the hypothesis would need to reach the gate, so this threshold is not set to force a pass.

protectedRationale: Caps exceed the largest per-arm run sd observed in the 2026-09/10 studies (typically 0.02-0.07) so noise cannot veto a real effect, while a regression beyond BOTH the cap and the pooled sd is still a legitimate rejection. The latency and token budgets admit the known ~2x cost of the second pass up front; exceeding them is a legitimate rejection, not an oversight. fake-citation influence is protected rather than targeted because the earlier study already asked about it and returned INCONCLUSIVE - re-asking it without new evidence would be re-litigating an unfinished experiment. whitespace stability is deliberately NOT protected: its pre-fix readings are meaningless, so capping a number that measures nothing would manufacture a false constraint.
adoptionRule: supported iff usable runs >= 2/arm at reliability >= 0.75 AND target "verbosity stability" moves up by >= 0.2 AND the bootstrap 90% CI lower bound of the signed improvement is > 0 AND no protected metric regresses beyond its cap AND pooled run sd. Fewer usable runs, any unmet condition or missing data => INCONCLUSIVE. Gate thresholds are untouchable.
budgetNote: NOT YET EXECUTED. scripts/judge-capacity.mjs refuses to start without an explicit provider call budget, and treats unknown capacity as insufficient. 312 jobs/run x 2 runs x 2 arms x 1.5 calls/job (the two-pass arm averages 2) x 1.25 retry allowance = 2340 expected calls; GO additionally requires the budget to cover 125% of that, i.e. >= 2925 calls. The free tier has not been observed at that size, so this study needs either several days of appended runs or a funded transport. Registered and sealed rather than started on hope.
